description: Groups — let the user edit recipients (targets), not just the group name. Extend updateGroup to validate and reconcile targets using the SAME semicolon 'email, Name;' convention as group create, and rebuild the raw-Tailwind group edit page into a semantic recipient editor. Independent of the other features. Keep the edit page functional and consistent in the semantic system; a full visual showcase of the group screens is a LATER phase — do not rabbit-hole on styling.
steps: In src/app/dashboard/groups/actions.ts extract the recipient parsing/validation from createGroup into a shared module-level helper `parseTargets(targetsText: string): { email: string; name: string }[]` that reproduces the current rules EXACTLY: trim; require the text to end with ';' (throw 'Every recipient entry must end with a semicolon (;)'); split on ';'; for each entry split on ',' → email = first part lowercased, name = rest joined; validate email with /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ (throw `Invalid email address: ...`); reject duplicates (throw `Duplicate email address: ...`). Refactor createGroup to use parseTargets so the two paths cannot drift.

Rewrite `updateGroup(formData)` in groups/actions.ts to reconcile targets: read id, name, targetsText; throw if id/name missing or targetsText blank; auth (createClient + getUser, throw 'Unauthorized' if none); FIRST confirm ownership by selecting `.from('groups').select('id').eq('id', id).eq('user_id', user.id).single()` — if not found throw; parse via parseTargets(targetsText); update the name `.from('groups').update({ name }).eq('id', id).eq('user_id', user.id)`; then reconcile with delete-then-insert for THIS group only: `.from('targets').delete().eq('group_id', id)` then insert parsed targets mapped with group_id: id (only if there is at least one); redirect(`/dashboard/groups/${id}`).

Rewrite src/app/dashboard/groups/[id]/edit/page.tsx into a SEMANTIC server component: await params; `const supabase = await createClient()`; auth redirect('/login'); load the group owner-scoped (.eq('id',id).eq('user_id',user.id).single()); notFound() if missing; load its targets `.from('targets').select('*').eq('group_id', id).order('email')`; serialize them to the editor format `targets.map(t => t.name ? `${t.email}, ${t.name};` : `${t.email};`).join('\n')`; render .content-page + .page-heading (eyebrow 'Groups', back link) with <EditGroupForm group={{ id, name }} initialTargetsText={serialized} />. Remove all indigo-*/gray-* Tailwind markup.

Create src/app/dashboard/groups/[id]/edit/EditGroupForm.tsx ('use client') reusing the create page's recipient-editor UX: copy the local parseTargets(value) used by groups/create/page.tsx for the live validation pill and inline errors; useState for name (seed group.name) and targetsText (seed initialTargetsText); render <form action={updateGroup} className='form-card'> with a hidden <input name='id' value={group.id}>, an 'Audience name' field, the .recipient-editor textarea <textarea name='targetsText'> with the validation-pill and .recipient-errors UX from create, a Cancel <Link> to `/dashboard/groups/${group.id}`, and <SubmitButton label='Save changes' pendingLabel='Saving group…' />. Use .content-page/.form-card/.form-section/.field/.recipient-editor/.validation-pill classes only.
acceptance_criteria: createGroup and updateGroup share one parseTargets helper (no duplicated/divergent validation).
updateGroup updates the name AND replaces the group's targets (insert new / remove deleted) scoped to that group_id, after verifying .eq('user_id', user.id) ownership.
Invalid or duplicate emails in the edit form are rejected with the same messages as create.
The group edit page pre-fills existing recipients in the semicolon format and uses semantic CSS classes (no indigo-*/gray-*).
npm run lint exits 0 and npm run build succeeds.
verification: Run `npm run build` — must complete with no errors.
Manually confirm updateGroup verifies ownership before deleting/inserting targets and that the delete is scoped to .eq('group_id', id).
findings: Extracted a module-level parseTargets(targetsText) helper in groups/actions.ts with the exact create rules (trim; must end with ';'; split on ';'; email=first comma part lowercased, name=rest; /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ validation; duplicate rejection) and refactored createGroup to use it so the two paths cannot drift. NOTE: because actions.ts carries 'use server', the helper could NOT be exported (Next.js: 'Server Actions must be async functions' — build failed on an exported sync fn); it is kept as a non-exported module-level function, which still satisfies the single-source/no-drift requirement. updateGroup now reads id/name/targetsText, validates presence, authenticates, FIRST verifies ownership via .from('groups').select('id').eq('id',id).eq('user_id',user.id).single() (throws 'Group not found' if missing), parses via parseTargets, updates the name scoped to .eq('id',id).eq('user_id',user.id), then reconciles targets with delete-then-insert scoped to .eq('group_id', id) (insert only when at least one), and redirects to /dashboard/groups/${id}. The edit page is now a semantic server component (await params; createClient; redirect('/login') when no user; owner-scoped group load; notFound() when missing; targets loaded via .eq('group_id',id).order('email') and serialized to `email, name;` / `email;` lines) rendering .content-page + .page-heading with a new client EditGroupForm. EditGroupForm ('use client') mirrors the create page's recipient editor: local parseTargets for the live validation pill + inline errors, useState seeded from group.name and initialTargetsText, <form action={updateGroup} className='form-card'> with hidden id input, Audience name field, .recipient-editor textarea (name='targetsText'), Cancel Link to /dashboard/groups/${id}, and <SubmitButton label='Save changes' pendingLabel='Saving group…'/>. Only semantic classes used (no indigo-*/gray-*). The back link uses className='eyebrow' to match the sibling templates/landing-pages edit pages. npm run lint exits 0 and npm run build succeeds. No scratch files created.
